paper.title: Exponential Regret Bounds for Gaussian Process Bandits with Deterministic Observations

settings.name_in_paper: Gaussian process bandits with deterministic observations
unmapped: objective f is a sample from a zero-mean GP with known kernel hyperparameters; function values observed exactly
queries restricted to a finite lattice L in D that is divisible by 2
kernel four times differentiable along the diagonal
settings.definition_quote: As in (Srinivas et al., 2010), the objective function is distributed according to a Gaussian process prior: f(x) ~ GP(m(.), kappa(.,.)). ... our assumption is that once the function has been probed at point x in D, then the value f(x) can be observed with very high precision.

algorithms.name: Branch and Bound (GP-UCB/LCB with search-space shrinking)

bound.regime: t > T_0 for some integer T_0

symbols.A: positive constant depending on the instance
symbols.tau: positive constant depending on the behaviour of f near its global maximum
symbols.T_0: integer threshold after which the bound holds (paper's T)

conditions: kernel four times differentiable along the diagonal

f a continuous GP sample with unique global maximum x_M satisfying (†) interior quadratic behaviour f(x_M)-c1||x-x_M||^2 < f(x) <= f(x_M)-c2||x-x_M||^2 on B(x_M,rho_0), or (‡) x_M on boundary with f and boundary smooth and grad f(x_M) != 0
lattice L satisfies 2L ∩ conv(L) ⊆ L and is fine enough to intersect B(x_M, rho_0) (condition (5))
tuning: beta_T = 2 ln(|L| T^2 / alpha) with alpha in (0,1)

source.quote: Then, there exist positive numbers A and τ and an integer T such that the points specified by the Branch and Bound algorithm, {xt}, will satisfy the following asymptotic bound: For all t > T, with probability 1 − α we have r(xt) < A e^{−τt/(ln t)^{d/4}}.

results.notes: Bound is on instantaneous regret r(x_t)=f(x_M)-f(x_t), not cumulative; quantity set to 'other'. Variable t mapped to T. Constants A, tau not explicit.

bound.expression_latex: \text{the cumulative regret is bounded from above}

source.quote: Given κ, f ∼ GP(0, κ) and L ⊆ D as in Theorem 2, the cumulative regret is bounded from above.

results.notes: Corollary only states cumulative regret is bounded (constant in T); probability type inherited from Theorem 2 (w.p. 1-alpha) presumably.
